Variables: Storage Boxes

Type + name + value. Store it, peek at it, swap it — the tag stays.

⏱ 15 min🧠 No experience needed🧪 Interactive
Step 1

One box, one food, one tag

Sticker = type, tag = name, soup = value.

🍱

Labelled lunchboxes. Type sticker (“soup only”), name tag (“Aarav’s”), today’s soup (value). Swap soup daily; sticker stays. Java’s auntie (compiler) refuses sandwiches in soup boxes.

= STORES, == asks. Single equals puts values in; double equals compares. Different jobs, different symbols.

Step 4
17 → 18 → 19
Run the swaps and watch.

      
ProgramRead each line in order

      
public class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    int age = 17;            // declare + initialize
    System.out.println(age); // 17
    age = 18;                // birthday: replace the content
    System.out.println(age); // 18
    age = age + 1;           // read, add, store back
    System.out.println(age); // 19
  }
}
Each print reads the CURRENT content. Old values vanish on overwrite.
